title: Controller Compatibility with Steam Deck and Handheld PCs
summary: Which controllers work with Steam Deck and handheld PCs? Learn about Bluetooth, USB-C, and 2.4GHz dongle connections for external gaming controllers.
body_markdown:
The Steam Deck and handheld PCs like the ASUS ROG Ally and Lenovo Legion Go come with built-in controls, but let's be real: sometimes you want a full-size controller. Maybe you are docked on a TV, running local co-op, or you just prefer the feel of a proper gamepad. Good news: most controllers connect without drama.


Here is everything you need to know about pairing an external controller to your Steam Deck or handheld gaming PC.


### Quick Answer


Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch Pro controllers all connect to Steam Deck via Bluetooth or USB-C. The Xbox Wireless Adapter is not natively supported on SteamOS, so Bluetooth is your go-to for wireless Xbox controllers. For the lowest latency when docked, use a 2.4GHz USB dongle. Windows-based handhelds like the ROG Ally support virtually every PC controller out of the box.


## Which Controllers Work with Steam Deck?


SteamOS is Linux-based, but Valve built broad controller support into the operating system. Most popular gamepads connect right out of the box.


Xbox controllers


connect via Bluetooth or USB-C. One catch is that the Xbox Wireless Adapter does not have native driver support on SteamOS, so Bluetooth is your wireless option. If you run into pairing issues, check your


[wireless controller connection settings](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/connect-wireless-xbox-controller) before troubleshooting further.


PlayStation controllers


(DualShock 4 and DualSense) pair via Bluetooth or USB-C. Steam Input handles full button remapping and touchpad support natively, which is a huge win for PS players going portable.


Nintendo Switch Pro Controller


connects over Bluetooth and Steam recognizes it without any extra setup.


Third-party PC controllers


that support USB or Bluetooth generally work fine on SteamOS. Linux compatibility varies with niche brands, so double-check before buying.


You can connect multiple


[controllers](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/controllers) at once for local multiplayer. Four Bluetooth controllers is the practical ceiling before connection stability starts getting shaky.


## How to Connect a Controller to Steam Deck


### Bluetooth Pairing


Head to Settings > Bluetooth on your Steam Deck. Enable Bluetooth if needed, then put your controller into pairing mode (hold the pairing button until the light flashes). Select the controller from the list, and you are good to go.


### USB-C (Wired)


Plug directly into the Steam Deck's USB-C port. SteamOS recognizes most controllers automatically. Using a dock? Plug into one of the dock's USB-A ports instead.


### 2.4GHz Dongle


Some


[wireless gaming controllers](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/controllers) use a 2.4GHz USB dongle for lower latency than Bluetooth. Plug the dongle into the Steam Deck's USB-C port using a USB-A to USB-C adapter, or into a docking station's USB-A port directly.


## Do Wireless Controllers Work with Steam Deck?


The answer is yes. Most wireless controllers connect over Bluetooth without issues, but the connection method you choose matters more than you might think.


Bluetooth connections can occasionally drop in areas with heavy wireless interference, and that gets worse when you are also running a Bluetooth headset at the same time. A 2.4GHz dongle sidesteps this entirely by delivering more stable input with lower latency. On the hardware side, per Valve's official specs, the Steam Deck LCD supports Bluetooth 5.0, while the OLED model upgraded to Bluetooth 5.3 with a dedicated antenna for improved connection reliability.


For docked gaming where you want rock-solid input, a controller with a 2.4GHz USB dongle is the better play. For portable sessions on the couch? Bluetooth handles it just fine.


## What About Other Handheld PCs?


Devices like the ASUS ROG Ally, Lenovo Legion Go, and MSI Claw all run Windows, so controller compatibility is much broader. Almost any gamepad that works on a Windows PC works with these handhelds without additional setup.


[Xbox controllers](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/xbox-controllers) connect via Bluetooth, USB, or Xbox Wireless Adapter.


[PlayStation controllers](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/playstation-controllers) work via Bluetooth or USB through Steam Input or DS4Windows. Most third-party


[PC controllers](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/pc-controllers) connect normally with zero hassle.


Windows handhelds also support the Xbox Wireless Adapter for the lowest-latency wireless connection to Xbox controllers, which the Steam Deck does not offer natively. With that broader compatibility, you can also take advantage of premium gamepads built for PC. A


[modular wireless controller](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/victrix-pro-bfg-reloaded-wireless-controller) with swappable components gives you even more flexibility since you can switch between stick layouts depending on the game.


## Can You Use a Controller While Steam Deck Is Docked?


Absolutely, and docking is actually the most common reason people reach for an external controller in the first place. When your Steam Deck is plugged into a TV or monitor through a dock, the built-in controls are not practical. A wireless controller lets you sit back and play like you would on a console.


Most docking stations pack multiple USB-A ports, so you can plug in a controller dongle and still charge the Steam Deck at the same time. For the best


[couch gaming experience](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/ultimate-couch-gaming-setup-wireless-controllers-with-30-foot-range) , pair a solid controller with a


[wireless headset](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/headsets) that connects directly to the dock or console for clean, lag-free audio. A


[dedicated wireless gaming headset](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-700-gen-3-headset?Platform=Xbox&Color=Black) with its own 2.4GHz transmitter avoids the Bluetooth bandwidth competition between your controller and audio entirely, and if you are weighing your options, understanding


[wired versus wireless audio quality](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/wired-vs-wireless-gaming-headphones-sound-quality-latency) helps you pick the right setup for docked play.


## Steam Input: Custom Controller Layouts


One of the Steam Deck's biggest strengths is Steam Input. You can remap every button on any connected controller on a per-game basis, adjust dead zones, and even map gyro controls to gamepads that support motion sensing.


Community-created controller profiles are available for most popular games, so you can download a layout someone else already optimized rather than building one from scratch. If


[stick drift](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/why-stick-drift-happens-gaming-controllers) is throwing off your inputs, adjusting dead zones through Steam Input is a quick software-side fix while you sort out the hardware.

Bluetooth Higher Good for portable play No


USB-C (Wired) Lowest Best No

## Conclusion


Most controllers work with Steam Deck and handheld PCs right out of the box. Bluetooth handles casual use well, while 2.4GHz dongles deliver better stability for competitive or docked play.


For Windows-based handhelds, Turtle Beach controllers like the


[Stealth Ultra](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-ultra-controller?Title=Default+Title) and


[Stealth Pivot](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-pivot-controller?Title=Default+Title) connect wirelessly via their 2.4GHz USB transmitters and deliver AntiDrift™ thumbsticks with hall-effect precision that holds up across thousands of hours. Both controllers also support Bluetooth for Android devices and supported Smart TVs, giving you flexible connection options across your setup. Once your controller is sorted, round out your docked rig with a


[lightweight open-back headset](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/atlas-air-headset?Title=Default+Title) for marathon sessions where comfort matters as much as sound.


## FAQs


### Do wireless gaming controllers work with Steam Deck?


Yes. Most Bluetooth controllers connect directly. Controllers with 2.4GHz USB dongles also work via the USB-C port (with a USB-A adapter) or through a docking station.


### Can I use a controller with Steam Deck while it is docked?


Yes. Docking and using an external controller is one of the most popular Steam Deck setups for TV gaming.


### Does Steam Deck support Bluetooth controllers out of the box?


Yes. The Steam Deck LCD has Bluetooth 5.0 and the OLED model has Bluetooth 5.3. Both support Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, and most third-party Bluetooth controllers natively.


### What controllers are compatible with other handheld gaming PCs?


Windows-based handhelds like the ROG Ally support virtually any PC-compatible controller via Bluetooth, USB, or Xbox Wireless Adapter.


### Do I need a dongle to connect a controller to a handheld PC?


Not always. Bluetooth works without a dongle. A 2.4GHz dongle provides lower latency but requires a USB port or adapter.


### Can I use multiple controllers on Steam Deck at once?


Yes. You can connect multiple Bluetooth or USB controllers for local multiplayer. Connection stability may drop with more than four Bluetooth devices connected simultaneously.
